subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Windows Companion select official `2026.7.2-beta.3` as its production default before an official OpenClaw artifact contains the wizard-runtime correction and passes the native setup proof?
rationale: The implementation can prove compatibility with a composed candidate, but only maintainers can accept a prerelease default whose actual published artifact is known to fail a core setup stage.

options.title: Wait for a proven official artifact
options.body: Keep the current production default until OpenClaw ships the correction, then require real Windows setup proof against that exact unmodified release.

options.title: Accept the beta limitation
options.body: Merge the beta.3 default while explicitly accepting that the documented wizard path remains unavailable until the upstream release lands.

options.title: Split the work
options.body: Land only the independently safe lifecycle, formatting, and candidate-proof work in a narrowed PR while leaving the production version selection unchanged.

recommendation.title: Wait for a proven official artifact
recommendation.body: Keep the current production default until OpenClaw ships the correction, then require real Windows setup proof against that exact unmodified release.

likelyOwner.reason: They were explicitly requested for review in the timeline and are the best available candidate for a release-policy decision.
